figure: Figure 15.2, left panel (a) 'Caching removes prefill work'
issue: The in-plot formula 'f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P)  P=40%, S=60%' uses symbols S and P that are never defined in the figure, caption, or adjacent prose. The drawn curve is consistent only if P is the reusable prefix share (f(10)=(0.6+0.04)/1.0=0.64, matching the plotted ~64; asymptote 60%=S). A competent reader who reads S as 'shared' (the natural reading) computes f(10)=(0.06+0.40)/1.0=0.46 and finds the formula contradicts the plotted curve — a plausible-but-wrong inference permitted by the figure.
evidence: Rendered PDF p. 259: green in-plot text 'f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P) P=40%, S=60%'; plotted green curve passes ~80 at r=2, ~70 at r=4, ~64 at r=10, ~61 at r≈50 (recomputed: (0.6+0.4/r)/1.0). Caption defines r ('average prefix reuse = mean number of requests served from each cached prefix block') but never defines S or P.
acceptance_test: Caption or an in-plot note defines the symbols explicitly (e.g., 'P = reusable prefix share of prefill work, S = non-reusable remainder'), or the symbols are renamed to self-documenting forms; recomputing f from the printed definitions reproduces the plotted values at r=2, 10, and the 60% asymptote.

figure: Figure 15.2, right panel (b) 'Decode goodput vs batch size'
issue: The red in-plot annotation asserts 'tail latency keeps rising' — a quantity that is not plotted on this figure and is not mentioned in the caption or the adjacent prose. The figure encodes goodput only; the tail-latency claim is an unshown, uncited qualitative assertion embedded in the visual.
evidence: Rendered PDF p. 259: right panel y-axis is 'Relative decode goodput (a.u.)' only; red annotation reads 'diminishing gains past ~b16 (no hard plateau): goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising'. Caption Scope line covers only the goodput curve ('illustrative (synthetic) curves, not measured benchmarks').
acceptance_test: Either the tail-latency statement is moved into the caption/prose as an explicitly qualitative expectation (e.g., 'qualitatively, per-request latency also rises with batch size — not plotted'), or a second encoded series/annotation basis is added; the bare in-figure assertion no longer stands without scope.

issue: Both series ('no cache' red, 'with prefix cache' green) use the same filled-circle marker; in grayscale the red and green luminances can be very close, so the legend entries are distinguished mainly by line position and text. The curves themselves remain separable by shape (flat vs. declining), so this is a robustness/polish issue, not a readability failure.
evidence: Rendered PDF p. 259: legend shows red line+circle for 'no cache' and green line+circle for 'with prefix cache'; the two series overlap only at r=1.
acceptance_test: Legend/series markers use distinct shapes (e.g., circle vs. square/triangle) so the two entries remain distinguishable in a grayscale printout; curves and labels otherwise unchanged.
